item.title: Iran warns US to stay out of Hormuz after Trump says US will ‘guide’ ships
item.description: Iran warned the US to stay out of the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump said the US will begin Project Freedom on Monday to guide stranded ships out of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Pakistan Says It Helped Transfer Iranian Crew From Ship That U.S. Seized
item.description: Pakistan helped transfer an Iranian crew from a US-seized ship back to Iran. Describing the transfer of the crew from the MV Touska cargo ship back to Iran as a ‘confidence-building measure’ between U. S.

item.title: Crew of Iranian ship seized by US forces evacuated to Pakistan, gov’t says
item.description: The crew of the Iranian ship MV Touska, seized by US forces, has been evacuated to Pakistan for repatriation. Twenty-two crew members were transferred for their return. Twenty-two crew members from the seized Iranian ship MV Touska have been transferred to Pakistan for repatriation.

item.title: Iran military says U.S. forces will be attacked if they enter Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran warns that US interference in the Strait of Hormuz will be considered a ceasefire violation. The warning comes from the Iranian parliament's national security commission. Any American interference in the new maritime regime of the Strait of Hormuz will be considered a violation of the ceasefire, says Iranian parliament's national security commission.

item.title: Japan PM says Iran war oil crisis having ‘enormous impact’ in Asia Pacific
item.description: Japan PM's minister Sanae Takaichi says the Iran war and oil crisis are having a significant impact in Asia Pacific. She made the comments during a visit to Australia. Sanae Takaichi makes comments during a visit to Australia, where she signs agreements on energy supplies.

item.title: Japan, Australia agree to deepen cooperation on energy, defence and critical minerals
item.description: Japan and Australia have agreed to deepen cooperation on energy, defence, and critical minerals. The two countries have significant trade ties, particularly in energy supplies. Australia provides almost half of Japan’s liquefied natural gas; Japan is one of Australia’s top five suppliers of refined gasoline and diesel.

item.title: China’s Global Security Report exposes fundamental flaws in Beijing’s worldview
item.description: China's Global Security Report reveals flaws in Beijing's worldview. The report has been made public, exposing these fundamental issues. China’s Global Security Report exposes fundamental flaws in Beijing’s worldview Firstpost.

item.title: Women in developing countries hardest hit by rising debt burden, UN research finds
item.description: UN research finds women in developing countries are disproportionately affected by rising debt burdens. They face increased financial hardship and vulnerability due to limited access to resources and support. Women in developing countries hardest hit by rising debt burden, UN research finds The Guardian.

item.title: United Airlines Flight Hits Truck While Landing At US Airport
item.description: A United Airlines flight carrying 221 passengers and 10 crew members hit a truck while landing at a US airport. The incident occurred during the landing process. The jet was carrying 221 passengers and 10 crew members.

item.title: United Airlines Jet Clips Lamppost And Truck Near Newark Airport
item.description: A United Airlines Boeing 767 carrying 231 passengers and crew clipped a lamppost and truck near Newark Airport. The plane landed safely with no injuries reported. The United Airlines Boeing 767 landed safely with 231 passengers and crew onboard, no injuries reported.

item.title: Detained Gaza aid flotilla activists arrive in Netherlands
item.description: Two activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla were released from Israeli custody and arrived in the Netherlands. They were part of a detained Gaza aid flotilla. Two activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla arrived in the Netherlands after being released from Israeli custody.

item.title: How the Kremlin Lures Africans Into Russia’s War in Ukraine
item.description: The Kremlin is luring African men into Russia's war in Ukraine with promises of jobs, only to force them into combat. Many are unwittingly drawn in as mercenaries or forced labor.

item.title: North Korea women's soccer club to make rare South Korea visit
item.description: South Korea will host a North Korean women's soccer club for the first time in eight years. The rare inter-Korean sports clash will take place this month in South Korea.

item.title: How “Pressure to Surrender” Traps Conflicts in Endless War
item.description: Modern Diplomacy published an article on how pressure to surrender can trap conflicts in endless war. The article explores the dynamics of modern conflict resolution. How “Pressure to Surrender” Traps Conflicts in Endless War Modern Diplomacy.

item.title: What to know about hantavirus, the illness suspected in a cruise ship outbreak
item.description: A hantavirus outbreak is suspected on a cruise ship. The illness is typically found in rodents and can be transmitted to humans through contact with infected animals. What to know about hantavirus, the illness suspected in a cruise ship outbreak.

item.description: Jeffrey Sachs discussed the global economic meltdown and its impact on Europe in a recent interview. Sachs warned of the potential consequences of economic instability. Jeffrey Sachs: Global Economic Meltdown & Destruction of Europe (Transcript) The Singju Post.

item.title: Trump says the U.S will 'guide' stranded ships from the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: President Donald Trump said the US will guide stranded ships from the Strait of Hormuz. Two ships reported attacks near the strait. The United States will launch an effort on Monday to "guide" stranded ships from the Iran-gripped Strait of Hormuz, President Donald Trump said, as two ships around the strait reported attacks.
